title: Serving a rendering
description: What a server must do to publish an instance's renderings truthfully. Derived from skills/folio-core/serving-renderings.md, which settles the contract and deliberately specifies no tool. Opened for bean folio-assistant-0hi8 / issue #363, where topologies whose `publication host` axis is not `github-pages` have no publication mechanism at all.
_comment: A requirement rather than prose in the skill because more than one tool may satisfy it, and #363 asks for 'several options'. Stating the obligations separately is what makes a second implementation checkable against the first instead of against the first's source.

statements.label: Serve each rendering with its declared media type
statements.requirement: A server MUST set Content-Type from the declared table in RENDERING_MEDIA_TYPES, not from the filesystem's extension map.
statements._comment: Measured 2026-09-19: python3 `mimetypes` and `Bun.file().type` BOTH already resolve .jsonld to application/ld+json, so the common claim that a general-purpose server cannot serve a rendering is FALSE and is not stated here. The real gap is `longest-extension-first`, below.

statements.label: `.schema.json` resolves before `.json`
statements.requirement: A server MUST resolve the longest matching extension first, so that `<stub>.schema.json` is served as application/schema+json and not as application/json.
statements._comment: The one row no OS media-type table carries, because `.json` is a suffix of `.schema.json` and nothing knows the compound extension means a schema. This is the whole substantive difference between a conforming server and `python3 -m http.server`.

statements.label: The bare stub resolves to the viewer
statements.requirement: A request for `<stub>/` MUST return that directory's index as text/html.
statements._comment: GitHub Pages resolves an extensionless URL only to a directory index, which is why the viewer is a directory at all. A local server that 404s here makes the two hosts disagree about a URL the documentation prints.

statements.label: `<stub>.json` is the same bytes as `<stub>.jsonld`
statements.requirement: Where both are published they MUST be byte-identical; a server MUST NOT synthesise one from the other.
statements._comment: An alias is only an alias while it is byte-identical. Two documents asserting the same IRIs is the defect --base-url exists to prevent.

statements.label: An undeclared file keeps the server's own inference
statements.requirement: For a path the declaration says nothing about, a server MUST fall back to its normal inference and MUST NOT force application/octet-stream.
statements._comment: The third state. 'The declaration says nothing about this file' is not 'this file has no type' — the same rule as readme-sections' skip and ci-health's could-not-check.

statements.label: Never serve outside the served root
statements.requirement: A server MUST NOT serve a file outside the directory it was pointed at, including via a symbolic link inside that directory.
statements._comment: Not inherited from the skill — added because the reference implementation failed it. Its own test pointed a link inside the root at a file outside and got 200: a lexical path check passes a clean URL, and resolve() never touches the filesystem. Real paths must be compared. This matters most for `self-sovereign`, which is `outward facing: no` and whose published directory sits next to data nobody intends to publish.

statements.label: Bind loopback unless told otherwise
statements.requirement: A server SHOULD bind a loopback interface by default, and expose a network interface only on explicit request.
statements._comment: SHOULD, not SHALL: a sovereign-cloud deployment is `outward facing: yes` and legitimately binds a public interface. Making this SHALL would encode a rule against a working setup.
